text:
alex: seeing intermittent DNS failures from GPU nodes in eu-west. model pulls to s3-backed buckets are intermittently failing with SERVFAIL. any recent egress/NAT changes?

priya: saw the same on the console. dns error rate up ~10x in the last hour, mostly from the edge egress pools. correlates with SNAT conntrack churn on the NAT gateway :thinking_face:

henry: grabbing a tcpdump from a node — looks weird: many DNS queries using identical source ports across different pods, and replies sometimes don't map back. snippet:

```
22:14:01.123456 IP 10.42.3.12.45987 > 8.8.8.8.53: 12345+ A? model-service.internal.example.com.
22:14:01.123457 IP 10.42.7.5.45987 > 8.8.8.8.53: 12346+ A? model-service.internal.example.com.
22:14:01.123458 IP 10.42.9.2.45987 > 8.8.8.8.53: 12347+ A? model-service.internal.example.com.
...
```

henry: responses from upstream occasionally show `SERVFAIL` or get dropped at the NAT when port mappings collide. looks like port-preserving NAT + source-port reuse is causing confusion.

alex: we're using kube-proxy (iptables) SNAT on nodes and our NAT gateway does port-preserving mappings to conserve ports. glibc resolver on pods does randomized source ports and `rotate` option is on in our resolv.conf — could be a collision/rate-limit interaction at upstream auths.

priya: here's resolv.conf from failing pod:

```
search staging.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local example.com
nameserver 10.0.0.2
options ndots:5 timeout:1 attempts:1 rotate single-request
```

priya: note `rotate` + low timeout/increased parallelism from many model-serving containers. prod has higher qps to the same auth and we might be tripping per-client rate limits.

lina: staging doesn't show it because staging egress uses per-node SNAT pools (no port preservation). production shares a small NAT pool across many nodes -> likely port exhaustion and collisions. also GPUs batch-start many pods at once which spikes concurrency.

devops-bot: ALERT: dns_error_rate exceeded on eu-west-edge-e1 (90s window) — 14% errors. See: https://console/alerts/1234

henry: short mitigations we should try (low-risk first):
- remove `rotate` from resolv.conf in the pod base image to reduce per-pod source-port churn (quick rollbackable).
- increase `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` on nodes to give larger ephemeral range: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range=\"15000 61000\"`.
- add `cache` TTL tweak in coredns to reduce query rate for hot names.

alex: longer term: expand NAT pool / disable port-preserving mode on the gateway, and add per-pod egress IPs for model fetch jobs. I'll prepare a canary patch to remove `rotate` from the pod base image and bump coredns cache TTL for eu-west. rolling tonight at 23:00 UTC. @lina can infra coordinate NAT pool expansion and a quick telemetry dashboard for dns-src-port distribution?

lina: on it. opening infra ticket, increasing NAT ephemeral pool by 2x and adding histogram metrics for source-port usage per egress node. also adding runbook entry: if DNS SERVFAIL spike correlates with src-port reuse -> scale NAT pool or switch to per-node pools. ETA for first roll: 3 hours.

alex: thanks — will post rollout notes and add a follow-up once canary is healthy.
